evidence.observation: Initial creation samples include DescribeContinuousBackups DISABLED and ContinuousBackupsUnavailableException for valid enable; another table initially returns TableNotFoundException from both backup APIs despite successful CreateTable and subsequent DescribeTable CREATING. RecoveryPeriodInDays 36 is rejected by ValidationException before backup readiness or table visibility. CreateTable returned CREATING, but only the later DescribeTable snapshot is a current lifecycle observation.

The no-op disable control has current DescribeTable CREATING snapshots around valid-disable unavailability. Later current DescribeTable ACTIVE snapshots at 54 and 58 bracket DescribeContinuousBackups DISABLED at 55, ContinuousBackupsUnavailableException at 56 for PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled false, and ValidationException at 57 for the same request plus RecoveryPeriodInDays 36. At 60, ContinuousBackupsStatus becomes ENABLED; the same valid no-op succeeds at 61 and is separately described at 62. ACTIVE is insufficient for readiness and no-op disable is not exempt.

The passive second generation makes no UpdateContinuousBackups calls until sequence 100. ContinuousBackupsStatus is DISABLED while CREATING and remains DISABLED across current ACTIVE snapshots 94/96/98, then becomes ENABLED at 99 without any PITR update. Its first no-op disable succeeds at 100. Background readiness does not require an update request; this small nonrandomized sample does not measure whether attempts accelerate or delay background work.

Current DescribeTable UPDATING snapshots at 28 and 31 bracket successful PITR disable at 30 on an already-ready table. ContinuousBackupsStatus stays ENABLED and separate description at 32 confirms PITR DISABLED. A blanket rejection for every non-ACTIVE table would contradict this operation-specific native behavior.

Current DescribeTable DELETING snapshots bracket successful no-op disable on ready tables. For the passive table a later DescribeContinuousBackups returns TableNotFoundException at 77. DELETING does not itself force UpdateContinuousBackups unavailability while the backup subsystem still recognizes the table; subsequent missing-table responses are a separate disappearance boundary. This capture does not enable PITR during deletion.

The fresh enable second generation repeatedly rejects valid enable while snapshots show CREATING and ContinuousBackupsStatus DISABLED. Sequence 174 describes CREATING, 175 describes backups DISABLED, 176 accepts enable with backups ENABLED/PITR ENABLED, and 177 describes ACTIVE. This transition straddles requests: it does not prove successful enable while the table remained CREATING, and this enable branch did not reproduce an ACTIVE unavailable request. Separate descriptions 178/180 confirm PITR ENABLED; disable at 181 and description 182 confirm PITR DISABLED before deletion.

Native ContinuousBackupsStatus exposes a sampled DISABLED-to-ENABLED readiness transition; no ENABLING state is observed or documented for this field. PITR remains DISABLED on both sides for disable/passive controls, with restore bounds and retention fields absent, so PITR status and its absent optional fields do not expose this transition. Readiness must be distinct from both general table status and user PITR enablement. Calls are sequential rather than atomic; no universal synchronization guarantee between describe and update is established.

All three owned names were reused only after verified absence. All final tables are absent. PITR DISABLED was described before each deletion; all before/after/final BackupType ALL inventories are empty without continuation tokens, and no backup was discovered or retained. The owned GSI used to exercise UPDATING was deleted before its source table after DeleteTable correctly rejected the in-progress index operation.

sources.observation: Documents ContinuousBackupsUnavailableException (HTTP 400): Backups have not yet been enabled for this table. Successful update returns the current ContinuousBackupsDescription. Prose says backups are ENABLED at table creation; native transient observations above distinguish accepted creation from readiness.
Checks continuous backups and PITR; documents TableNotFoundException and up to 10 calls per second. Probe request cadence stays below this bound.
ContinuousBackupsStatus valid values are ENABLED and DISABLED, not ENABLING.
PITR status valid values ENABLED and DISABLED; restore timestamps and retention are optional.
Describes table lifecycle states separately from backup readiness; explicitly allows deleting a CREATING index while Backfilling true.

limitations: Observed elapsed times describe these calls only and are not a readiness timer or AWS guarantee. Three names with two fresh table identities each are a bounded sample, not a statistical latency study.

The initial generation close-sampling loop was interrupted by shared Python Eval globals: two malformed nonmutating requests went into replica_autoscaling_api.json and received UnknownOperationException before TypeError. No named resources crossed over. This capture contains only the three owned names. The initial first ACTIVE samples are delayed; uninterrupted second-generation sampling uses an isolated subprocess.

No ENABLING field value was observed. DISABLED-to-ENABLED correlates with this sample readiness boundary, but sequential requests do not prove an atomic oracle or exclude further native propagation windows.
Passive readiness establishes updates are unnecessary. This small nonrandomized sample cannot prove attempts never influence scheduling or estimate their latency effect.

The UPDATING control uses one empty on-demand table and a transient owned GSI; no items, restores or capacity changes were introduced. DeleteTable during CREATING GSI was rejected; cleanup deleted the backfilling index then the table.
Initial backend visibility and final disappearance can differ between DescribeTable and continuous-backup APIs. General table status alone is not the operation eligibility predicate.

No continuous-backup unavailable window duration is promoted to an implementation timer. A production lifecycle must own backup readiness independently of user PITR state and table lifecycle, with operation-specific visibility/eligibility and validation ordering.
